 Brandon Thomas-Asante of Coventry City warms up ahead of the match with Tottenham Hotspur. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Brandon Thomas-Asante of Coventry City warms up ahead of the match with Tottenham Hotspur. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty Images Daniel Harris Mon 19 Oct 2026 14.46 EDT First published on Mon 19 Oct 2026 13.30 EDT Share Key events 46m ago Teams 
 1h ago Preamble 
 43s ago 14.46 EDT De Zerbi tells Sky that Spurs have injuries and he likes putting players in their best positions, so Gray and Maddison will both play midfield. Savio and Bergvall played well in Manchester but are injured, while Udogie felt his knee so they didn’t want to take a chance on him.
 Spurs had a training camp in Marbella last week, which was important for his vision to create relationships and mentality in the team.
 Share 6m ago 14.41 EDT Dignity! 
 Cristiano Ronaldo receives 30-day suspension and £215 fine over Portugal walkout Read more Share 9m ago 14.37 EDT Coventry, meanwhile, will know Van Hecke lacks pace, so I’d expect Cherif to play on him while, in behind, Rudoni takes chances, gambling with ambitious passes and shots. If Tosin is indeed at right-back but even if he isn’t, Dasilva and Sakamoto will look to double-up down the left, while Yirenkyi and Grimes restrict the central spaces Spurs will be hoping to control. If their wide players are brave enough to keep the width, they can make chances tonight.
 Share 15m ago 14.32 EDT Where is the game? Spurs will look to dominate possession, with Gray and Tonali dictating play, so Maddison, Kudus and Marmoush can buzz about behind Solanke. The absence of a proper winger means they’ll probably look to create centrally, Solanke attacking space for little balls in behind, before going wide to put crosses into a well-populated box.
 Share 23m ago 14.23 EDT “None of this is De Zerbi’s fault,” reckons Dave Estherby, “yet lose tonight and surely, he’s toast.” 
 I’m not sure about that. I’m guessing, but I’d be shocked if, when he took the job, he didn’t insist on certain levels of spending and control. On top of which, he picks the team, so I’d say some of their failings can be attributed to him, but I’d be shocked if he gets the flick, even with a defeat tonight. My impression is the board have committed to him and, given the underlying data isn’t terrible, I expect them to stick with their man.
 Share 28m ago 14.18 EDT Spurs’ principal problem so far this season has been scoring goals. De Zerbi is famed as Mr Buildup and seems to have inculcated decent method in his charges. But he can’t stick their chances away for them and, in Dominic Solanke, they have a 29-year-old striker who, if we’re being honest, has put together one serious season in his career. I wonder if anyone regrets selling Troy Parrott.
 Share 31m ago 14.15 EDT Thinking a little bit more about the Spurs formation, I find it hard to believe De Zerbi sticks Maddison in a two-man midfield – in ant event, but all the more so after so long out. BBC reckon it’ll be 3-4-2-1, but my sense is Tosin plays right-back and has been included to guard against Coventry’s aerial threat.
 Share 34m ago 14.12 EDT Email! “Quick point of order about the preamble,” says Kieran McHugh. “Basically correct until the last sentence. As a Spurs fan I can attest that this will not be fun.”
 That’s exactly what makes it fun.
 Share 36m ago 14.11 EDT I guess it’s possible Spurs stick with four in defence, but it’d mean Tosin playing right-back, which seems unlikely; we shall see.
 Share 38m ago 14.09 EDT Just the one change for Coventry, meanwhile: Ephron Mason-Clark drops to the bench, with Tatsuhiro Sakamoto coming in for his first Premier League start.
 Share Updated at  14.43 EDT 39m ago 14.08 EDT Taking a closer look, the headline news for Spurs is that James Maddison makes his first start in 536 days, while Dejan Kulusevski is in the matchday squad for the first time in 526 days. And if we want another number, they’re the only team in the top six divisions yet to have won a game this season. 
 Otherwise, by the looks of things, Roberto De Zerbi has to three at the back, with Tosin Adarabioyo coming in for his first Premier League start, while Andy Robertson and Omar Marmous also come in; dropping out are Marcos Senesi, the injured Destiny Udogie, Lucas Bergvall, and the also injured Savio.
 View image in fullscreen A fan holds a sign aloft in honour of Dejan Kulusevski. Photograph: Javier García/THFC/Shutterstock Share Updated at  14.39 EDT 46m ago 14.01 EDT Teams
 Tottenham Hotspur (3-4-2-1): Kinsky; Tosin, Van Hecke, Van de Ven; Gray, Tonali;, Maddison, Robertson’ Kudus, Marmoush; Solanke. Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Tel, Fernandes, Kulusevski, Davies, Olusesi, Williams-Barnett.
 Coventry City (4-2-3-1): Rushworth, Van Ewijk, Thomas, Pinnock, Dasilva, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Thomas-Asante, Cherif. Subs: Bentley, Simms, Mason-Clark, Mluni, Awoniyi, Onyeka, Kesler-Hayden, Torp, Hamer.
 Referee: Andy Madley (Huddersfield)
 View image in fullscreen The Four Kinsky’s. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Share Updated at  14.37 EDT 1h ago 13.30 EDT Preamble
 Sport’s ability to ape and shape the world means it teaches us many things, often in a friendlier environment than real life. It is, for example, better to learn the Australian states and their capitals during an Ashes series than by rote in a geography lesson, just as the accordant failure and disappointment is – ultimately! – less painful to process when it’s happening to yet another bunch of hapless tourists than when it’s happening to us.
 Football, though, is a slightly different thing, the constant competition and the way in which teams are passed down through families installing their nature as part of our personalities, both heirloom and genetics. And within that, there’s supporting Tottenham, a relentless barrage of dark nights and false dawns delivering martyrdom to the afflicted and mirth to everyone else.
 Even in context, though, a summer spend in excess of £300m, to go from fourth-bottom to bottom, is exceptional behaviour, suggesting a malaise too encoded to alleviate. But it is also the case that their performances have been better than three points from six games suggest – which might be viewed as integral to the nature of it all, or might indicate an imminent upturn.
 Tonight’s match will give us a decent idea as to which interpretation is accurate. Coventry – whose fans understand a misery far beyond the conception of Spurs types – arrive in N17 following an uplifting thrashing of Newcastle. As such, they will be confident, physical and beatable or, in other words, exactly the kind of outfit against which Spurs are prone to fail. A win tonight would take Frank Lampard’s men up the table from 16th to 11th but, more than that, with home games against Fulham and Sunderland coming up next, it could set them up for the season. This should be fun…
 Kick-off: 8pm BST
